label: Game B
nuance_found: Drifting (steer plus handbrake tap) banks points and a combo multiplier, and smashing signs and bollards adds to it, while going off the road costs speed and a magnet drags you back. A hint at about 150 s says chains of drifts bring dawn closer. I never saw a real trade-off beyond 'drift more, crash less'.
audio: Generated wind and ambience with a busy burst of notes at the start, then mostly quiet driving sounds and smash effects. No tune I could hum.
furthest_progress: Drove about 44 miles (score 15,380, clock 01:55 after wrapping past midnight, no dawn reached) through night and rain; best chain was a x2 drift multiplier and an 11-smash combo worth 1,850
control_trouble: Steering with a virtual gas slider at 70-90 mph was twitchy for my clumsy thumb and I left the road many times; a live thumb might do better. The gas slider seems to accept a small left or right nudge only.
best_moment: Drift through a rainy bend with lights streaking and signs flying, with the score ticking up.
worst_moment: Sliding off the road and waiting 5 to 8 s for the magnet to pull the car back, again and again, with no clear goal.
verdict: Gorgeous, honestly the best-looking thing I have seen on my phone this month, with a night drive, rain and cherry blossom trees. But I did not know what I was supposed to do for the first two minutes. There is no level, no star, no target I can see, just a score and a clock. I kept running off the road and being dragged back by a giant magnet, which killed the flow. I would admire it for 90 seconds and then delete it for something with a goal. Maybe I would give it another go for the drifting if someone showed me how.
